title: I used to ...
subtitle: I used to work / she used to be
summary: Use used to + verb to say what happened often or was true before, but is not true now.

lesson.heading: Dave used to work in a factory
lesson.text: A few years ago Dave said: 'I work in a factory.' Today Dave says: 'I work in a supermarket. I **used to work** in a factory.' So Dave **used to work** in a factory = he worked in a factory before, but he doesn't work there now.

examples.text: Dave **used to work** in a factory. Now he **works** in a supermarket.
When I was a child, I **used to like** chocolate.
I **used to read** a lot of books, but I don't read much these days.

lesson.heading: The form
lesson.note: **used to** is the same for every subject.

lesson.heading: More examples
lesson.text: We use **used to** for things that happened many times before, and also for things that were true before but are not true now.

examples.text: A woman holds an old photo of herself with very long hair. She says: 'I **used to have** very long hair.'
Liz has got short hair now, but it **used to be** very long.
They **used to live** in the same street as us, so we **used to see** them a lot. But we don't see them very often these days.
Helen **used to have** a piano, but she sold it a few years ago.

lesson.heading: Negative and questions
lesson.text: The negative is **didn't use to ...** and the question is **did you use to ... ?** Here we write **use to**, with no *d*.

examples.text: When I was a child, I **didn't use to like** tomatoes.
Where **did** you **use to live** before you came here?
What games **did** you **use to play** when you were a child?

lesson.heading: used to and the present

left.label: used to = the past only
examples: We **used to live** near the airport.

right.label: present simple = now
right.text: For now we use I play / he lives etc.

lesson.note: You cannot say ~~I use to play golf~~ or ~~We use to get up early~~ about now.

lesson.text: *used to* has no present. For things that are true now, use the present simple: *Mary watches TV every evening*.

exercises.prompt: A man is showing a photo of himself as a young footballer. He says: 'When I was younger ...' He ___ football.
exercises.explanation: He played football before, but not now: he used to play football.

exercises.prompt: A woman says: 'I'm a hairdresser now.' In her old photo she is standing next to a taxi. She ___ a taxi driver.
exercises.explanation: used to + be for something that was true before.

exercises.prompt: Is the sentence about before (not now) or about now?

items.text: He used to work in a factory.
Liz's hair used to be very long.
I used to read a lot of books.

exercises.prompt: A couple say: 'We live in London now.' Their old photo shows their house in the country 20 years ago. They ___ in the country.
exercises.explanation: They lived there before, but not now.

exercises.prompt: This building is a shop now, but a long time ago it was a hotel. This building ___ a hotel.
exercises.explanation: In positive sentences we write used to + verb.

exercises.prompt: Match the two halves of each sentence.

pairs.left: Dave used to work in a factory.
pairs.right: Now he works in a supermarket.

pairs.left: Liz's hair used to be very long.
Helen used to have a piano.
pairs.right: She sold it a few years ago.

pairs.left: I used to read a lot of books.
pairs.right: I don't read much these days.

pairs.left: They used to live in our street.
pairs.right: We don't see them very often now.

exercises.prompt: Karen works very hard and has no free time now. A few years ago she swam every day. She ___ every day.
exercises.explanation: used to + swim, for something she did often before.

exercises.prompt: 'Have you got a car?' 'No, I ___ one, but I sold it.'
exercises.explanation: She had a car before, but not now: I used to have one.

exercises.prompt: When I was a child, I never ___ meat, but I eat it now.
exercises.explanation: I never used to eat meat = before I didn't eat meat.

exercises.prompt: Mary loves watching TV. She ___ TV every evening.
exercises.explanation: This is true now, so we use the present simple: she watches.

exercises.prompt: Ask your friend about the games in her childhood.
exercises.answer: What games did you use to play when you were a child?
exercises.explanation: In questions we use did + use to (with no d on use).

exercises.statement: I used to play tennis. These days I use to play golf.
exercises.explanation: I used to play tennis. These days I play golf. used to is only for the past.
